reviews.comment: 420 is coding heavy but it's all straight forward with the way Dr. Walsh sets it up. She provides step by step instructions and is easy to contact if something is wrong. Attendance is mandatory and there's a daily quiz question at the end of every lecture. She's also very sweet and takes her time explaining things during lecture.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor clearly cares so much about the class. Grade is made up about 80% of coding assignments and 20% attendance. Workload is high but relatively not very difficult, so just be prepared to devote some time. The coding assignments have about 10-20 pages of instructions.  Overall, the assignments are easy to follow and structured very well.

Every class began with a short lecture followed by a worksheet in which you had to collaborate with 2 other people and finally a 2-question quiz. Therefore, there was a LOT of busy work because of the sheer amount of worksheets. There were 4 exams (non-cumulative final) and 4 opportunities for extra credit. Easy class but a bit much for a 100 level
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor, however, the class is not as easy as it looks. Tests are worth 65% of your total grade, so try not to fail and it should be fine. Participation matters as there are clicker questions and quizzes mostly every class.

Honestly an amazing professor, she cares about her students. The exams were not difficult at all although sometimes the concepts were not too easy to understand. Pretty easy class overall though and gives 4 whole points on semester average for extra credit. Would definitely recommend her. Don't skip though as she has clicker questions every class.

Participation will literally make it break your grade. Exam 4 is the final which is nice but the workload throughout the year is a bit much. Participation and short quizzes using iClicker every. single. class. Nice professor though.

her review lectures before the exam are very helpful. attendance is not mandatory but most days we had iclicker questions or quizzes, so you need to show up in order to get credit for those. extra credit is easy to get, but the workload can be a little heavy.
Easy A class as long as you show up to lectures and do the homework

Overall this class was fairly simple. The tests were sometimes hard, they are multiple choice & fill in the blank. Every class there are clicker questions and a quiz at the end that is 2 questions. If you skip class you miss those points. There is also homework every week but its pretty easy and useful for the tests. Theres lots of extra credit.

Professor Walsh made this my least stressful class. Work load is not a lot; at least not outside of class. Attendance is definitely required because you have quizzes, clicker participation and worksheets throughout the class (that are locked to be due in class). Tests are easy if you study her power-points. COVID friendly as well (offers masks).

Reads straight out of the PowerPoint. the textbook is required and expensive. There is little homework. Her exams are average. There is a quiz and an assignment every class, so if you miss class your grades will drop. Not to mention an exam is 65% worth of your grade so if you mess up in one it can be brutal to your GPA.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is great this class is really interesting and she is always willing to stay back and answer questions after class, the exams arent too bad they are about half multiple choice and half fill in the blank, there are clicker quizzes and participation questions almost every class, so it is def important to attend class.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Walsh is very helpful and flexible. I was having problems with my iClicker, and she negotiated a fair solution with me. Her lectures are long, but in between topics, the class does worksheets and quizzes to reinforce new material. Definitely take this class if you have an interest in astronomy, and make sure to turn in homework.

She is ok. The course went into some rather difficult concepts, and to her credit she simplified it somewhat during lectures enough for you to get the idea, most of the time. Her tests are 67% fill in the blank (which is harder than it seems) and 33% MC. Not too much homework, and offers 4 points max of EC. Not the most fun class but a solid one.

She was alright. It was a really dry course. There were several times events in the astronomical field happened and she made no mention of them; it was a missed opportunity to really get people interested and apply things taught in class to the real world. 4 exams, 30mc and 30 fill in the blank. Theres online homework, and daily clicker quizzes.

Professor Walsh is pretty dope. The exams are basically what she covers in lecture and form the book so its not too ad. There is a fill in the blank section on every exam, but it isn't too bad as long as you know your stuff. There are quizzes almost everyday in class, so make sure you stay up to date on the information. She offers extra credit also
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her tests come straight from the PowerPoints in class, which she posts on eCampus! Offers extra credit to your course grade throughout the semester. Tremendous knowledge of the material and accessible outside of class. Take her class for interesting lectures and an easy science credit.

There are in class quizzes everyday that count for your participation grade and y-our quiz grade. There's a test every two weeks over two chapters. The mastering astronomy homework was easier than the tests. I wouldn't take this class again.

The tests were easy; the Mastering Astronomy homework (although there wasn't a lot of it) was hard. Don't come to class tired because you will fall asleep. I found the material interesting, though, so I was okay. She'll answer any semi-related space question you have during class, which is cool. There's some easy partner work and in-class quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY
